title: Copilot Studio: app- and intent-first agent creation experience
summary: Hold: the briefing treats data-policy protection as unconfirmed even though Microsoft documents its application to Copilot Studio agents in scoped environments. It also presents an environment credit allocation as a spending cap without explaining that linked pay-as-you-go billing can allow consumption to continue.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes an app- and intent-first agent creation experience in Microsoft Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot Studio: Introducing an App- and Intent-First Agent Creation Experience

claims.claim: Microsoft plans an app-first experience in which makers start with the application their agent will work with and configure its capabilities.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio is evolving to an app-first agent creation experience. Makers start with the application their agent will work with and configure the capabilities it needs.

claims.claim: The planned update brings tools and knowledge into a more unified agent creation and configuration experience.
claims.quote: This update brings tools and knowledge into a more unified experience, simplifying how agents are created and configured.

claims.claim: The documented Microsoft Copilot harness creation sequence has makers name the agent, write instructions, save, then add knowledge, tools, skills and connected agents from the Build tab.
claims.quote: Your agent opens in the agent designer with the Build tab active and the name field in focus. ... After saving, you can continue to build your agent:

claims.claim: Knowledge is the data an agent can access when answering user questions.
claims.quote: Knowledge is the data your agent can access when answering user questions.

claims.claim: A tool blocked by data policy cannot be selected in the current Add a tool dialog.
claims.quote: When a data policy blocks a tool, the tool appears unavailable in the Add a tool panel and you can't select it.

claims.claim: Some tools require makers to sign in or provide credentials.
claims.quote: Some tools require you to sign in or provide credentials before you can use them.

claims.claim: The data-policy entry point is Power Platform admin center > Security > Data and privacy > Data policy.
claims.quote: On the sidebar, select Security, and then select Data and privacy. The Data protection and privacy page opens. ... Select Data policy. The Data policies list appears.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Agents, workflows and apps powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness use usage-based billing measured in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Agents, workflows, and apps powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness and customer conversations handled by Microsoft Contact Center Intelligence use a usage-based billing structure.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness billing starts when makers begin building, unlike the standard harness, which starts billing after publishing.
claims.quote: Unlike the standard harness, which starts billing after publish, the Microsoft Copilot harness charges credits from the moment you start building.

claims.claim: Building, previewing and evaluating Microsoft Copilot harness agents consume Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness consume Copilot Credits while makers build, preview, and evaluate them, before those agents enter a formal production lifecycle.

claims.claim: Credit allocations are reached through Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Licensing. ... Under Products, select Copilot Studio, and then select Manage Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 is the allocation-write endpoint.
claims.quote:
$apiBaseUrl = "https://api.powerplatform.com"
$apiVersion = "2024-10-01"
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put `
    -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion"

claims.claim: Administrators can cap an environment's consumption at its Copilot Credits allocation.
claims.quote: When you clear this option, the environment doesn't draw from unallocated prepaid capacity in the tenant after it consumes its allocation. If the environment is linked to a pay-as-you-go billing plan, usage can continue through the linked Azure subscription.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'Administrators can allocate prepaid Copilot Credits to environments and turn off Draw from the available capacity in my tenant to cap prepaid consumption at the allocation. Usage can still continue through a linked pay-as-you-go billing plan.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/manage-usage-github-copilot-harness.

claims.claim: Environment allocation controls determine allocated credits and whether the environment can draw from tenant capacity.
claims.quote: The Draw from the available capacity in my tenant option in the admin center maps to the TenantPool enforcement rule
claims.fix: Add to the row note: 'If a published environment group rule governs Draw from the available capacity in my tenant, the setting cannot be overridden for an individual environment.'

claims.claim: Managing credit allocations requires the Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.
claims.quote: Sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.claim: Environment capacity controls apply to all Copilot Studio workloads in an environment, not just Microsoft Copilot harness agents.
claims.quote: Environment capacity controls apply to all Copilot Studio workloads in the environment, not only agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness.

claims.where: Governance controls; controls[1].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Whether existing environment capacity controls govern workloads created through the new experience is unconfirmed and depends on whether it uses the Microsoft Copilot harness.
claims.quote: Power Platform admin center capacity and consumption controls apply across Copilot Studio. They aren't exclusive to agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness.
claims.fix: Replace the credits row note with: 'Environment capacity controls apply across Copilot Studio to credit-consuming workloads, regardless of harness; this creation flow's harness and building charges are not yet documented.' Replace 'Microsoft has not confirmed that either one governs the new creation experience' with 'The new creation screens are not yet documented; existing data-policy and capacity controls retain their documented platform scope.' Remove 'in case the new flow is billed on the Microsoft Copilot harness' from the credit-allocation checklist item.

claims.claim: The change specifically replaces the first screen makers see with the screen where they choose tools and knowledge.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio app-first creation; intent-first knowledge. Opened build-new-agent and whats-new. The roadmap promises an app-first, more unified experience but does not identify a first screen or locate tool and knowledge selection on it.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence with: 'The roadmap describes a different starting point for makers and a more unified experience for tools and knowledge.'

claims.claim: Administrators can review environment credit consumption in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: To view credit consumption across an environment or your tenant, go to Licensing > Copilot Studio in the Power Platform admin center.
